title.narrative: Specialized GBV, and General Protection Services in Dinsoor and Qansax Dheere (Bay Region)

description.narrative: ltpgtDignity First Somalia (DFS) proposes specialized protection project to enhance access to lifesaving protection services for conflict- and disaster-affected populations in Dinsoor, and Qansax Dheere districts, located in Bay regions. These areas have been significantly impacted by protracted conflict, climate shocks, forced displacement, and a breakdown in social protection systems, placing vulnerable populations—especially children, women, and minority groups—at heightened risk of violence, exploitation, abuse, and neglect.ltbrgtThe project will deliver an integrated package of Gender-Based Violence (GBV), and General Protection services to an estimated 6000 individuals. A significant portion of the target population are internally displaced persons (IDPs), female-headed households, survivors of GBV, and persons with disabilities. These groups continue to face severe barriers to accessing protection services, compounded by stigma and absence of functioning referral systems.ltbrgtInterventions will be delivered by trained protection caseworkers embedded in the community and will be aligned with national SOPs and inter-agency referral pathways.ltbrgtFor GBV prevention and response, DFS will provide specialized case management services to 800 GBV survivors, including psychosocial support, safety planning, and referrals for legal and health services with up to 2,700 individuals. Case management of rape (CMR) will be strengthened by supplying essential kits (PEP) to health facilities in coordination with the Health Cluster and GBV AoR. The project will also integrate cash-based support in GBV case management, allowing survivors to access lifesaving services, relocate when necessary, and mitigate protection risks. GBV services will be survivor-centered, confidential, and adhere to GBV guiding principles.ltbrgtThe General Protection component will serve 2,300 individuals in Qansax Dheere through mobile and static protection desks offering legal assistance, individual protection assistance (IPA), and referrals based on individualized protection assessments. The project will also establish and strengthen community-led protection structures that identify at-risk individuals—especially persons with disabilities and minority groups—and link them with appropriate services. This will enhance community-level protection mechanisms and support self-reliance in emergency contexts.ltbrgtAcross all interventions, DFS will ensure strong community engagement, representation of women and persons with disabilities, and accountability to affected populations. Protection mainstreaming, including disability inclusion, Do No Harm, and PSEA (Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse), will be integral to project design and implementation. DFS will leverage existing networks of social workers, protection actors, and community-based organizations to ensure effective outreach and referral mechanisms.ltbrgtThis project aligns with the 2025 Somalia Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan and contributes to the protection cluster’s objective to reduce protection risks and respond to the urgent needs of conflict-affected and displaced populations. It prioritizes life-saving, high-impact activities that address both immediate and longer-term protection concerns through a survivor-centered, rights-based, and inclusive approach.ltbrgtlt/pgt
